open_obligations: Note that Michael et al.'s AI consultants were much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer; check which model Khan et al.'s consultants use and how strong they are.
Check the size of Khan et al.'s incorrect-consultant accuracy drop, and whether it is reported for human judges, LLM judges or both.
Check that judge interaction is allowed in both consultancy setups.
in.other_title: Judge interaction does not raise debate accuracy; incorrect consultants mislead
in.rationale: Michael et al. report dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time on QuALITY-hard. Khan et al. report that in consultancy incorrect experts cause low judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy. Michael et al. also found judges reach 87% accuracy with dishonest AI consultants, which they explain at least in part by their AIs being much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer, so the support comes from Michael et al.'s human consultants rather than their AI consultants.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether dishonest consultants mislead human judges in hidden-passage QuALITY consultancy

text: Splitting consultancies by consultant honesty, the paper reports that dishonest human consultants successfully deceive judges 40% of the time, while for AI consultants judges do better when the consultant is dishonest (87% accuracy) than when honest (74%). The authors attribute higher AI-consultancy accuracy at least in part to the AIs being much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer.
title: Dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time; judges do better against dishonest AI ones
